_meta.title: Family and Friends 4 — Curriculum Map
_meta.note: Covers Grade 3→4 transition. All 8 units + 4 review sections catalogued.

units.title: Free time!
vocabularySets: Hobbies (skateboarding, cycling, hiking, photography, gardening, birdwatching, collecting, doing puzzles, painting, cooking)
Opinions and feelings about activities (love, enjoy, like, don't mind, dislike, hate)
units.grammar: like / love / hate / enjoy + -ing (gerunds); How often...? + frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never)
units.phonics: Long a sound (rain, play, day, eight, they, break, weight)
units.values: Making the most of free time and trying new activities
units.readingSkill: Reading a hobbies survey or profile
units.writingSkill: Writing about your hobbies and free time
units.speakingTask: Interview a partner about their favourite hobbies
units.listeningTask: Listen to children talking about hobbies and complete notes
units.project: Make a 'My Hobby' poster or mini-book
units.cultureLink: Popular free-time activities in English-speaking countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 different hobbies and activities
Express likes and dislikes using gerunds
Ask and answer 'How often do you...?' questions
Use frequency adverbs correctly in sentences

units.title: Wild weather!
vocabularySets: Weather adjectives (foggy, icy, stormy, humid, boiling, freezing, mild, breezy, overcast, drizzly)
Extreme weather events (flood, drought, hurricane, blizzard, heatwave, thunderstorm, tornado, avalanche)
units.grammar: Comparative adjectives (hotter than, more dangerous than, less cold than); as...as
units.phonics: Long e sound (sea, green, easy, these, theme, even, between)
units.values: Being aware of weather safety and climate change
units.readingSkill: Reading a weather report or climate fact file
units.writingSkill: Writing a comparison of two seasons or cities
units.speakingTask: Compare weather in different places using comparatives
units.listeningTask: Listen to a weather forecast and note key information
units.project: Create a weather diary or climate comparison chart
units.cultureLink: Extreme weather events around the world
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 weather conditions and describe them
Name and describe extreme weather events
Form and use comparative adjectives correctly
Compare two things using as...as

units.title: On the move!
vocabularySets: Means of transport (train, tram, ferry, cable car, hot air balloon, motorbike, scooter, submarine, speedboat)
Travel verbs and phrases (depart, arrive, board, get on/off, check in, fasten seatbelt, miss, catch)
units.grammar: Present continuous (is/are + -ing): actions happening now AND scheduled future arrangements
units.phonics: Long i sound (night, write, sky, fly, high, light, bright, find)
units.values: Travelling safely and respecting the environment while travelling
units.readingSkill: Reading a travel itinerary or transport timetable
units.writingSkill: Writing about a journey or travel plan
units.speakingTask: Describe what people are doing in a busy transport scene
units.listeningTask: Listen to travel announcements and note details
units.project: Plan a dream trip — create a travel poster with transport info
units.cultureLink: Public transport systems in the UK, USA, and Australia
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 types of transport
Use present continuous for current actions and future plans
Ask and answer questions in the present continuous
Understand and use travel vocabulary in context

units.title: Let's go shopping!
vocabularySets: Clothes and accessories (coat, scarf, gloves, boots, tracksuit, uniform, dungarees, cap, belt, earrings)
Shopping language (price, discount, receipt, change, afford, try on, size, fit, in stock, out of stock)
units.grammar: be going to (plans and intentions); going to questions: What are you going to...?
units.phonics: Long o sound (road, know, home, show, boat, old, most, phone)
units.values: Spending money wisely and buying only what you need
units.readingSkill: Reading a shopping dialogue or advertisement
units.writingSkill: Writing a shopping list or description of an outfit
units.speakingTask: Role-play a shopping conversation in a clothes store
units.listeningTask: Listen to a shopping dialogue and note the items bought
units.project: Design and describe your dream outfit or school uniform
units.cultureLink: Shopping habits and fashion trends in different countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 clothes and accessories
Use shopping language in a role-play context
Form going to sentences for future plans
Ask and answer questions with going to

units.title: Yummy food!
units.topic: Food groups, cooking, and healthy eating
vocabularySets: Food groups and types (grains, dairy, protein, legumes, vegetables, fruit; cereal, yoghurt, tofu, lentils, spinach, mango)
Cooking methods and kitchen equipment (boil, fry, bake, grill, steam, roast, blend; pot, pan, oven, frying pan, knife, chopping board)
units.grammar: Countable and uncountable nouns; some / any; How much...? / How many...?
units.phonics: Long u sound (cube, huge, music, view, beautiful, fuel, February)
units.values: Eating healthily and reducing food waste
units.readingSkill: Reading a recipe with step-by-step instructions
units.writingSkill: Writing a simple recipe or daily meal plan
units.speakingTask: Plan a healthy meal — discuss ingredients and quantities
units.listeningTask: Listen to a cooking programme and note the ingredients used
units.project: Create a class recipe card for a favourite dish
units.cultureLink: Traditional dishes and eating habits in English-speaking countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name foods from all main food groups
Distinguish countable from uncountable nouns
Use some, any, how much, and how many correctly
Write and follow a simple recipe

units.title: What a day!
vocabularySets: Irregular past simple verbs (went/go, came/come, saw/see, ate/eat, bought/buy, rode/ride, swam/swim, ran/run, fell/fall, won/win)
Time expressions for the past (yesterday, last week, last month, ago, the day before yesterday, in the past, once upon a time)
units.grammar: Past simple (regular and irregular verbs); past simple negatives and questions (didn't, Did you...? / What did you...?)
units.phonics: ar sound (car, farm, hard, start, large, heart, dark, sharp)
units.values: Cherishing good memories and learning from the past
units.readingSkill: Reading a diary entry or recount of a past event
units.writingSkill: Writing a diary entry or recount of a memorable day
units.speakingTask: Tell a partner about a fun day out using past simple
units.listeningTask: Listen to someone recounting a memorable event and answer questions
units.project: Make a 'My Best Day Ever' scrapbook page
units.cultureLink: Holidays and special events in English-speaking countries
keyLearningObjectives: Form and use past simple (regular and irregular) correctly
Make past simple negatives and questions
Use time expressions for the past accurately
Write a structured recount of a past event

units.title: Stay healthy!
units.topic: Body, health problems, and giving advice
vocabularySets: Parts of the body (shoulder, elbow, wrist, ankle, knee, hip, thumb, spine, chest, heel)
Health problems and treatments (cut, bruise, blister, sprain, rash, fever, headache, stomachache; bandage, plaster, ice pack, medicine, rest)
units.grammar: should / shouldn't (giving and receiving advice); What's the matter? / You should... / You shouldn't...
units.phonics: or sound (corn, form, short, horse, sword, ward, court, thought)
units.values: Taking care of your body and helping others when they are unwell
units.readingSkill: Reading a health advice article or first-aid leaflet
units.writingSkill: Writing advice for a friend with a health problem
units.speakingTask: Role-play: a friend is ill — give advice using should/shouldn't
units.listeningTask: Listen to a doctor giving advice and note the recommendations
units.project: Make a 'First Aid Tips' poster or booklet
units.cultureLink: Healthcare and healthy living tips from around the world
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 parts of the body
Describe common health problems
Give advice using should and shouldn't
Role-play a health consultation

units.title: Our planet!
vocabularySets: Natural wonders and landforms (rainforest, coral reef, glacier, volcano, canyon, waterfall, cave, delta, tundra)
Environmental problems and solutions (pollution, deforestation, global warming, habitat loss, recycling, solar energy, conservation, reforestation)
units.grammar: can / can't (present ability and possibility); could / couldn't (past ability)
units.phonics: er/ur/ir sounds (bird, girl, work, turn, heard, earth, early, journey)
units.values: Caring for the planet and taking action to protect wildlife
units.readingSkill: Reading an environmental article or wildlife conservation report
units.writingSkill: Writing a short report on an environmental issue and solution
units.speakingTask: Debate: what can we do to help the planet?
units.listeningTask: Listen to a nature documentary clip and answer questions
units.project: Create an 'I Can Help the Planet' action plan poster
units.cultureLink: Environmental movements and conservation projects worldwide
keyLearningObjectives: Name natural wonders and landforms
Describe environmental problems and suggest solutions
Use can/can't for present ability and possibility
Use could/couldn't for past ability

fluencyTimeSections.scenario: Talking to a new friend about hobbies and favourite activities
Planning a shopping trip with a friend
Telling a story about a memorable day out
Discussing ways to help protect the environment
